Compute school- and district-level performance trends

Source: R/aggregate_helpers.R
compute_performance_trends.Rd

Aggregates student_results_long to the school and district level and computes summary statistics, year-over-year changes, improvement classifications, school-level regression slopes, rank orders, year-to-year correlations, and intraclass correlations (ICCs). ICC computation requires the lme4 package (in Suggests); if not installed, $icc_tables is an empty data frame.

Usage

compute_performance_trends(
  data,
  spec,
  min_n_school = 10,
  improvement_threshold = 3,
  correlation_flag_threshold = 0.85
)

Arguments

data

A long-format student results data frame (see data contract).

spec

Named list describing the assessment program (assessment_spec).

min_n_school

Integer. Schools with fewer students than this in a year × subject × grade cell are suppressed. Default 10.

improvement_threshold

Numeric. Percentage-point change threshold for classifying a school as improving or declining. Default 3.

correlation_flag_threshold

Numeric. Year-to-year Spearman r below which a year pair is flagged as unstable. Default 0.85.

Value

A named list:

  • $school_level_summary — school × year × subject × grade with N, mean_score, sd_score, p05–p95, n_proficient, pct_proficient, yoy_change, demographic proportion columns, and yoy_change_score

  • $district_level_summary — district × year × subject × grade

  • $improvement_classification — school × year × subject: classification

  • $regression_slopes — school × subject × grade: slope, se, r_squared

  • $year_to_year_correlations — year_pair × subject × grade: pearson_r, spearman_r, n_schools, flagged

  • $rank_order_data — school × year × subject × grade: rank, pct_rank

  • $icc_tables — grade × subject × year: icc, var_between, var_within
